issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a Milkable.messageOnMilk() method with no parameters (returning a String like "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"), but the solution defines Milkable.messageOnMilk(double volume) (and implementing classes Seal and Goat implement messageOnMilk(double)). This parameter mismatch prevents students from implementing or using the interface as specified in the assignment and will cause compilation/signature mismatches when following the template/specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem statement and template: change the Milkable interface method signature to String messageOnMilk() (no parameters) and update Seal and Goat to implement messageOnMilk() returning "[Animal Type] [name] is milked". Alternatively, if the volume parameter is intended, update the problem statement, UML, and template Main calls to document and use messageOnMilk(double volume).

issues.description: The problem specification and UML define Milkable.messageOnMilk() as a no-argument method returning a String (expected return: "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"). The solution, however, defines Milkable.messageOnMilk(double volume) (a different signature) and the implementations in Goat and Seal include the volume in the returned string (e.g., "Goat [name] is milked ([volume]L)"). This signature and return-value mismatch between the problem statement and the provided solution creates a mapping confusion for students: they are instructed to implement a no-arg messageOnMilk() returning a simple "is milked" phrase, but the solution requires/uses a method with a double parameter and different formatting.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature and expected return across artifacts. Either: (A) Change the solution so Milkable.messageOnMilk() is a no-argument method returning "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" and update Goat and Seal to implement this no-arg method, or (B) Update the problem statement and UML to specify messageOnMilk(double volume) and document the volume formatting in the expected return. Option A is recommended to match the current exercise description.
